findings.title: Optimized paginator treats datetime keys as numbers
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this class to order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py around the optimized self.paginate call). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page dies in build_cursor with TypeError, and any later cursor compares an int to a timestamp column in SQL. The endpoint should keep DateTimePaginator (or this class must use DateTimePaginator's multiplier and fromtimestamp conversion). As written, optimized_pagination=true always 500s for admins.

findings.title: Negative queryset slices are invalid in Django
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log path always passes True) and the cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with that negative start (queryset[start_offset:stop]). Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError if start or stop is negative; it does not "handle negative slicing automatically" as the comment claims. A client-supplied cursor such as "0:-5:0" therefore 500s instead of paginating. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), so a negative prev offset now fails on every endpoint that uses BasePaginator, not only audit logs.

findings.title: Shared paginator silently clamps negative forward offsets
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result previously sliced with the cursor offset unchanged. It now uses max(0, offset) whenever the cursor is not a previous-page cursor. A crafted or corrupt forward cursor with a negative offset used to error; it now returns the first page as if offset were 0, with Link headers computed from that wrong slice. This runs for every BasePaginator consumer (issues, events, etc.), not just the new audit-log flag, and can repeat or skip rows without the client knowing the cursor was rejected.

findings.title: No tests for the new pagination branch
findings.body: The optimized_pagination query-param branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator are untested. Existing audit-log tests still hit DateTimePaginator, so they will not catch the datetime key TypeError, the negative-offset ValueError, or the cursor format change (DateTimePaginator encodes milliseconds; the new class emits raw numeric keys). A request with optimized_pagination=true from a superuser or global-access member should be covered before this path is exposed.
